implementation_notes: Go's persistence libraries hand you freshly decoded structs (database/sql Scan, GORM, ent, sqlc), so there is no session identity map to lean on and the classic structure is written by hand: the session/unit-of-work struct owns a map[Key]*Entity, the loader checks it first and inserts on a miss, and callers receive the same pointer for the same row. Store pointers, not values, or the map hands out copies and defeats shared identity; scope the map to one request/unit of work (pass it explicitly, e.g. through context.Context) rather than a package-level variable. Use sync.RWMutex or sync.Map only when the session really is shared, since Go's usual discipline is to confine a session to one goroutine.
pitfalls: Caching values instead of pointers silently defeats the map: each Get hands out a fresh copy with independent state.
A package-level map shared by all requests is an unbounded, stale cache; keep the session explicit and per request.
Only loads routed through the session are registered - a direct db.QueryRow elsewhere forks identity, so keep one repository as the single load path.
